verify_before_render: Meta announced Muse Spark Open 2026-10-15: 816B total/42B active, 1M-token context, natively multimodal; Meta calls it the most capable US open-weight model (vendor claim).
Weights downloadable under the Muse Model License with limited commercial terms — never call it Apache or unrestricted.
Press reports (TechCrunch/Engadget/Times of India): local runs need about 1 TB of RAM, e.g. two Mac Studios with M5 Ultra. It does not run on a normal Mac; say so.
Visuals are our own cards; no third-party clips. No on-screen credit captions.

scenes.heading: META'S *816B* GIANT
scenes.say: Meta just released the weights of its biggest model ever, tuned for Apple silicon.

scenes.heading: MEET *MUSE SPARK OPEN*
scenes.say: It is Muse Spark Open, which Meta calls its most capable open-weight model yet.

scenes.heading: HOW *BIG*
scenes.label: total parameters · 42B active · 1M context
scenes.say: Over eight hundred billion parameters in total, and only a slice of them works on each token.

scenes.heading: WHAT IT *DOES*
scenes.say: It is built for complex coding and long, multi-step agent work, and it takes text, image, video and audio.

scenes.heading: GET *ACCESS*
scenes.say: Use it through the Baseten or Fireworks APIs today, or download the weights yourself.

scenes.heading: BEFORE YOU *DREAM*
cons: ~1 TB of RAM to run locally
scenes.say: The catches: running it locally needs about a terabyte of memory, think two maxed-out Mac Studios, and the Muse licence limits some business use. In return, you get a million-token context.
Would you run a model this big at home? Comment MUSE and I will pin the announcement.

youtube.title: Muse Spark Open: Meta's 816B Giant Needs 1 TB of RAM
youtube.description:
Meta's Muse Spark Open is an 816B-parameter open-weight model (42B active, 1M-token context, natively multimodal) built for coding and agentic work. Meta calls it the most capable US open-weight model (their claim). The catch: local runs reportedly need about 1 TB of RAM — two Mac Studios with M5 Ultra chips — and the Muse Model License limits some commercial use.
Sources: TechCrunch (2026-10-15) and Meta's announcement.
